content.comment_body: Hello, I have two greenhouses, each equipped with a [product_name] controller. Both setups are identical, so the programs on each [product_name] are the same. On my HMI, I need one screen for each greenhouse with identical buttons since the control logic is the same. The only difference is the IP addresses ([product_name] 1: 192.168.2.5, [product_name] 2: 192.168.2.6). I’m able to connect to only one [product_name]. I’ve already created a connection called [product_name]_A for the first controller but cannot set up a second connection called [product_name]_B for the second one (see attached image). Can anyone tell me what I might be doing wrong? Thanks a lot!
Could you upload your HMI project as a zip file?

You have configured the same IP address for both [product_name] controllers in your connections. Update the connection for [product_name]_B to use the other IP, for example, change from 192.168.2.5 to 192.168.2.6.

Sorry, I'm not sure I fully understand. Where exactly should I change the IP address for the second [product_name]? I’ve checked all the menus but only see my HMI and one [product_name]—the second [product_name] isn't shown, so I can't adjust its IP.
Please refer to the attached screenshots...
OK, thanks! That was much simpler than I expected. I appreciate your quick responses.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced difficulty connecting a single HMI panel to two identical [product_name] controllers due to confusion over configuring separate device connections with distinct IP addresses. The main issue was unclear steps in the HMI software for setting up multiple controllers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects an intuitive way to configure and manage multiple controller connections within the HMI project, so that each can be assigned the correct IP address and both can be conveniently operated from a single HMI panel.
